title: The Ranger Who Got Struck by Lightning Seven Times
note: The seventh 3D short (2026-11-19). Planned STORY AND WORLD FIRST (caaleb, 2026-11-19: "you just realize you're much more writing a story now. Building a world that the viewer has to believe in"): one ranger, one mountain park, one storm, one run home from his lookout to his truck. Each fact lands on a moment of that run. Made under store/fresh.py and store/story_world.py.
lines: Right now, lightning is flashing about a hundred times every second, somewhere on Earth.
And it hunts for the tallest thing around. The Empire State Building gets hit about twenty-five times a year.
One park ranger, Roy Sullivan, got struck seven different times, and lived through every single one.
Every bolt is hotter than the surface of the sun, hot enough to turn sand into glass.
But your car protects you. Not the rubber tires, the metal shell. Would you stay inside?

sets_why: one park, walked top to bottom: the ridge where the storm hits first, the lookout tower that is the tallest thing on it, the forest trail down, the lake beach at the bottom, the trailhead lot where his truck is
ideas: the storm rolls over the ridge, a bolt splits the old oak beside the ranger and he dives flat; his truck sits tiny far below
he scrambles down the lookout tower's stairs as bolt after bolt slams into the rod on its roof above him
on the trail down he gets struck again and again and keeps marching, the trail markers counting him up to seven
at the lake a bolt hits the beach at his feet and he hauls a long branching glass root out of the sand
he slams himself into his truck, a bolt hits its roof, sparks race over the metal shell, and he knocks on the window at us from inside, grinning
storyboard: 1 hook (the ridge at last light, WIDE: the ranger whole on the bare crest, his lookout tower behind, the old oak beside him, his green truck tiny in the valley far below): storm clouds roll over the ridge and the light drops; his ears and hat brim lift with static and he looks up; a blinding bolt slams into the old oak beside him; the oak's crown splits and crashes down in flames as he dives flat into the grass.

2 the tallest thing (the steel fire-lookout tower in the rain, LOW: looking up the tower's zigzag stairs at him): the ranger bursts out of the cab at the top and runs down the stairs; a bolt slams into the lightning rod on the roof above him; sparks rain down past him as two more bolts hit the rod one after another; he jumps the last flight, lands, flicks his hat back onto his head and runs for the trail, straight past the camera.

3 seven times (the pine forest trail in the rain, TRACKING beside him as he marches downhill): the ranger marches down the trail; a bolt knocks his hat off and he snatches it back; strike after strike hits him while the numbered trail markers he passes count 1, 2, 3 ... up to 7; smoking and frazzled, he jams the hat back on and keeps marching.

4 hotter than the sun (the lake beach below the forest, HIGH: looking down on him and the sand): a bolt slams into the sand right in front of the ranger; the strike crater glows orange and steams; he grips and heaves; a long, branching glass root pops out of the sand and he tumbles back holding it up, glinting.

5 your shelter (the trailhead lot in the rain, CLOSE on his truck's side window): the ranger runs across the wet lot, yanks his green truck's door and slams himself in; a bolt hits the truck's roof; blue sparks race over the whole metal body around him and leap off the bumper into a puddle while the tyres stay dark; inside, untouched, he knocks twice on the window at us with a big grin and spreads his palms: see? would you stay inside?

world.logline: A park ranger's run home through the worst storm of the year: from his fire lookout on the ridge, down the forest trail and along the lake, to his truck at the trailhead.
world.hero: Data as the park's ranger: his lab coat under a ranger's flat-brimmed campaign hat, which he keeps losing and getting back
world.goal: get from the lookout to his truck before the storm gets him
world.place: one mountain national park: a bare ridge with an old oak and a steel fire-lookout tower, a pine forest trail switchbacking down, a lake with a sand beach, and the gravel trailhead lot where his green ranger pickup waits
